Sumimi v0.5.1 — **the site owner can now make us throw the crawlers away,
the way Umami does**.

v0.5.0 rebuilt the identity and made Umami's own tracker talk to Sumimi. This
one is small: a switch, and the note that says what it costs.

**`SUMIMI_STORE_BOTS=0`** ⇒ the crawlers are **dropped at the door**: the rows
never exist, the way Umami drops them (`isbot` ⇒ `{beep:"boop"}` ⇒ nothing is
written).

The default is unchanged — a crawler is **kept and marked** (`bot-ai-…`,
`bot-se-…`, `bot-social-…`, `bot-other-unknown`), and the marked traffic is
left out of the numbers unless the dashboard asks for it.

| | on (the default) | `SUMIMI_STORE_BOTS=0` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the rows | **in the database**, marked | **do not exist** |
| the disk and the writes | crawlers can outnumber the humans a hundredfold — keeping them is what that costs | **not paid** |
| "how many AI crawlers came?" | **answerable** | **not answerable** |
| the numbers | no crawlers in them | **no crawlers in them either** — the same numbers |

**The answer still carries the token.** A crawler that is dropped gets the same
`{cache, sessionId, visitId}` as everybody else, so the client cannot tell the
difference and its session continues. (Umami answers `{beep:"boop"}` with no
token at all, so its client's session starts over.)

**The same string decides both things.** The marker comes from
`ua::bot_kind(agent)` and the dropping comes from the same call on the same
string — so the two can never disagree about what a crawler is.

**Why the default is "keep them"**: keeping them is what makes the question
answerable at all, and keeping them costs disk — which is the side the site
owner can choose to save. The superset is not "we store more for you"; it is
"the capability is there, and whether you use it is yours".
